neighbours.label: a word praising how appealing an idea, theory or plan seems ('intuitively attractive', 'an appealing theory', 'seductive in its simplicity'), usually before a 'but'; the same adjectives for physical things stay low
fire: Many economists find the proposal intuitively appealing, though the data do not support it.
The theory that diet alone explains the trend is attractive, but it is almost certainly wrong.
Her explanation is elegant and appealing, which is exactly why we should test it carefully.
The notion that one gene controls intelligence is seductive in its simplicity.
To voters the promise of lower taxes and better services was an attractive idea.
It is a very appealing hypothesis, and I would like it to be correct.
The plan to rebuild the city in five years had an obvious emotional appeal.
At first glance the argument for a single global currency looks attractive.
quiet: Many economists find the proposal intuitively confusing, and the data do not support it.
The house that we visited on Sunday is attractive, but it is far too expensive.
Her new coat is warm and appealing, and it was cheap at the winter sale.
The notion that one gene controls intelligence was rejected by most biologists.
To tourists the old harbor with its painted boats was an attractive place.
It is a very attractive garden, and the roses bloom twice a year.
The plan to rebuild the city in five years was approved by the council.
At first glance the young actor in the photograph looks attractive.
